question.question: After an eligible Accept is acknowledged with the requested ballot, does the acceptor report at least ACCEPTED support in a later higher-ballot Prepare response, absent any intervening value replacement or decision?
question.importance: Recovery distinguishes accepted support from tentative preacceptance; misreporting acknowledged support can allow re-formation where the consumer should retain accepted attributes. This check targets local support accounting, not a whole-cluster disagreement.

question.trigger_rationale: Source shows a concrete producer/consumer mismatch: handleAccept sends matching-ballot acknowledgments after writing support but omits Status=ACCEPTED, while handlePrepare reports Status and handlePrepareReply explicitly branches on ACCEPTED. A real slow-path prefix distinguishes whether preceding paths already provide the missing status. This is more informative than re-running the explained codec or testing optional persistence without restart authority.

obligation.description: When an acceptor handles an eligible Accept for an uncommitted instance and emits an AcceptReply matching the requested ballot, a subsequent Prepare response for that instance must report support at least at ACCEPTED status, provided no intervening value-replacement transition has occurred. A higher promise alone must not erase the acknowledged acceptance phase.

scope.description: Local retention/reporting of acknowledged acceptance across a subsequent higher Prepare in static-membership volatile EPaxos.
assumptions: Valid Accept emitted by the implementation slow path
Request ballot at least current promise; instance not committed/executed before Accept
No intervening command replacement, restart or Commit delivery before Prepare

grounding.derivation: S-formation counts exact-ballot AcceptReply toward commitment and the owner marks its own state ACCEPTED before bcastAccept. S-recovery reports stored status and treats ACCEPTED separately from PREACCEPTED/NONE, preserving accepted support through an Accept path. S-try explicitly explains that accepted/committed state must not regress to preaccepted. These composed responsibilities require the acknowledging acceptor to retain/report its accepted phase; retaining only the ballot cannot substitute because the recovery consumer branches on Status. This is an implementation-derived support-preservation requirement, not an assumption that every Accept input must succeed.
grounding.applicability: Eligible valid slow-path Accept with a matching acknowledgment; later Prepare only raises promise.
